title: Chuckles rediscovered in Germany
summary: Green says Chuckles, taking Mosley's place in the Three Chocolateers, was rediscovered by a German woman and became known as Jimmy Chuckles Walker; they wrote to each other.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, like they used to demonstrate these tournaments. They acquired themselves a better -- a greater brotherly love, I would call it. And they was always hoping that someday maneuvers would arrive and gather them all together in some kind of mania. And fortunately, it happened to happen to me, you see. And I was talking about -- thinking about how could I do -- what would I do without Chuckles, you see, because Chuckles was -- he was back in the business. But he had got in the situation that I was in in the hospital, you know. He had to pinch hit, you see.

So, he took some fellow's place named Mosley. He used to be in the Three Chocolate-teers. And, well, he got rediscovered. Some woman imported a fraulein over in the fatherland, father-land, and they called her Gesler Gunther, you know. And she happened to see him, or some of her managers or somebody saw the Chocolate-teers over there with -- I think it was something about the Joy Train or something. Duke Ellington, you know.

And she liked the way he was -- his impressions, you know. He was so impressive, you see, because he's tall and he really was what they call -- I call a true slim, you know, because I mean he's -- I couldn't blame the lady, you know. She's fortunate, you see. You see, I thought I was lucky enough to have a friend like that as a child, you see, and to grow up with. But, I mean, you know so much for -- but he became like Jimmy Chuckles Walker, see. He got a chance to use his whole family name, you see.

Well, anyhow, I mean he started to be like some kind of producer. They made him a mascot of her office, I think. That's what I hear. They got some kind of portrait -- picture in the office of him as some kind of mascot.
Yeah. Well, I didn't loose touch, you know. I found out where he was. We wrote. We communicated, you know, but I was supposed -- on the way to a surprise. I was

going to be surprised by -- like the George Wein office, you see. He's some kind of -- in America he's supposed to be some kind of jazz leader, you know. I mean he represents jazz, like the jazz festivals, you know. Like the Newport Jazz Festivals.
And he had a friend, a great author that used to be a professor in the Mark Hunter College. But he passed on, you know. And --
That's Professor -- it's Jean Stern's husband.
